planting.note: Direct sow fresh acorns in fall, or plant container stock, in dry, infertile, sandy or rocky soil in full sun; Chapman's oak is a clonal, thicket-forming scrub oak of central Florida's ancient ridge scrub, including the Lake Wales Ridge.

directions: Plant young container-grown specimens in dry, infertile, sandy or rocky soil in full sun, ideally in fall or early spring; Chapman's oak is one of the key low-growing oaks of Florida's ancient scrub and scrubby high pine communities, including the Lake Wales Ridge, forming dense thickets by root suckering rather than growing as a single-trunked tree. Its small, leathery, evergreen leaves and compact multi-stemmed habit make it useful as a drought-proof informal hedge, windbreak, or wildlife thicket in a xeric native garden, and its acorns are an important food source for Florida scrub-jays and other scrub wildlife. Once established in lean sandy soil it needs no irrigation or fertilizer and tolerates the periodic fire that naturally maintains its native scrub habitat.

planting.note: Plant container-grown shrubs in spring into lean, rocky or caliche, well-drained, alkaline soil in full sun; Texas lignum vitae is a slow-growing, long-lived shrub of the Tamaulipan thornscrub and South Texas brush country.

directions: Plant container-grown shrubs in spring into lean, rocky or caliche, well-drained, alkaline soil in full sun; Texas lignum vitae is a slow-growing, long-lived shrub of the Tamaulipan thornscrub and South Texas brush country, usually staying a dense 5-8 foot mound but occasionally reaching small tree size with age. Clusters of fragrant violet-purple flowers with prominent yellow stamens open intermittently from spring through fall and draw abundant native bees, followed by small orange seed capsules that split to reveal shiny black seeds relished by birds. Its wood is exceptionally dense and was historically valued commercially, so cultivated nursery stock helps take pressure off wild populations; established plants need no irrigation beyond rainfall and shrug off the heat, drought, and poor soils typical of South Texas gardens.

planting.note: Plant container-grown shrubs in spring in rocky, caliche, or sandy, well-drained soil in full sun; goatbush is a stiff, intricately branched, spine-tipped shrub of the Tamaulipan thornscrub and South Texas brush country.

directions: Plant container-grown shrubs in spring in rocky, caliche, or sandy well-drained soil in full sun; goatbush is a stiff, intricately branched, spine-tipped shrub of the Tamaulipan thornscrub and South Texas brush country that forms dense, low thickets valuable for wildlife cover. Small reddish flowers appear in spring, followed by bright red, bitter berry-like fruit that is largely passed over by mammals but used by some birds, and the intensely bitter bark and foliage have a long history of folk medicinal use in the region. It tolerates extreme heat, drought, and alkaline soils with no supplemental care once established, and its thorny habit makes it a useful component of an impenetrable native hedge or thornscrub restoration planting.

planting.note: Plant container-grown shrubs in spring in well-drained, caliche or sandy loam soil in full sun; brasil is a thorny, multi-stemmed shrub to small tree of the Tamaulipan thornscrub and South Texas brush country.

directions: Plant container-grown shrubs in spring in well-drained, caliche or sandy loam soil in full sun; brasil is a thorny, multi-stemmed shrub to small tree of the Tamaulipan thornscrub and South Texas brush country, forming dense thickets valued for wildlife cover and as an informal native hedge or screen. Clusters of tiny greenish-yellow flowers in spring give way to small blue-black drupes that ripen in late summer and fall, heavily used by mockingbirds, cardinals, and other resident and migratory birds, and occasionally gathered locally for jelly. It is extremely drought- and heat-tolerant once established, needing no irrigation or fertilizer, and its dense thorny branching makes it a cornerstone shrub of South Texas brushland restoration and wildscaping projects.

planting.note: Plant container-grown trees in spring in well-drained, caliche, sandy, or loamy soil in full sun; tenaza is a thorny, fern-leaved small tree of the Tamaulipan thornscrub and Rio Grande Plains.

directions: Plant container-grown trees in spring in well-drained, caliche, sandy, or loamy soil in full sun; tenaza is a thorny, fern-leaved small tree of the Tamaulipan thornscrub and Rio Grande Plains, producing rounded clusters of fragrant cream-white puffball flowers in late spring and summer that draw abundant native bees and other pollinators. Flat, leathery seed pods follow the blooms and persist into winter, and the airy, feathery foliage casts light shade well suited to a thornscrub hedgerow or wildlife corridor planting. It is extremely drought- and heat-tolerant once established on the caliche and sandy soils typical of South Texas brush country, and regional habitat-restoration programs rely on it as a foundational thornscrub species.

planting.note: Plant container-grown shrubs in spring in well-drained, sandy, loamy, or caliche soil in full sun to light shade; Texas swamp privet is a dense, twiggy shrub of South Texas brush country, often along resacas and thornscrub margins.

directions: Plant container-grown shrubs in spring in well-drained, sandy, loamy, or caliche soil in full sun to light shade; Texas swamp privet is a dense, twiggy, multi-stemmed shrub of South Texas brush country and the Rio Grande Plains, often found along resacas, arroyos, and thornscrub margins rather than true standing wetlands despite its common name. Inconspicuous small greenish-yellow flowers open very early in spring before the narrow leaves emerge, followed by small blue-black drupes eaten by songbirds. Its dense twiggy habit makes it useful as an informal native hedge or screening thicket, and once established it tolerates considerable heat, drought, and mildly saline or alkaline soils typical of South Texas brushland with no supplemental irrigation.
